cite27: According to the Office of the Brooklyn Borough President, CD6 is below its targets for density in areas suitable for more housing, relative to most Brooklyn neighborhoods.

items.x: CD6 has the highest unit loss in Brooklyn and the fourth highest citywide (after Manhattan Community Districts 2, 7, and 8), with 1,500 units lost to consolidations from 2010–2024.

y26.x: Increase budget allocations for affordable housing construction and subsidies in areas experiencing the most need and displacement pressure, like Red Hook and Gowanus.

items.x: BKCB6 seeks to address natural affordability, increased accessibility, and aging-in-place within market rate housing through multifamily preservation programs and incentives, as well as promoting additional density through adaptive reuse or new development within contextually rezoned and landmarked parts of the district to accompany industrial rezonings.

y26.x: There is demand for responsibly developed market-rate housing that complements the district's infrastructure and affordability needs.

items.t: Enhance our subway and bus infrastructure
items.x: Fund accessibility upgrades, such as elevators and ramps, at key subway stations serving CD6. Accessibility improvements are broadly needed; other than the 7th Avenue F/G station, no stations within CD6 are currently served by elevators. CD6 also lacks east-west bus service, and there is widespread support to reactivate the B71 route, which was discontinued in 2010.

y26.x: Fund accessibility upgrades, such as elevators and ramps, at key subway stations serving the district, especially at the Smith-9th Street subway station, which lacks elevators despite being the highest elevation transit station in the entire world.

items.pr: Invest in Infrastructure for Climate Resilience and Transportation
items.t: Increase traffic enforcement to improve public safety
items.x: Hardened universal daylighting, coupled with dedicated loading zones are needed to increase visibility and safety and reduce commercial double parking which endangers pedestrians, cyclists and motorists. BKCB6 also supports the increase of red-light, speed, and bike-lane cameras at priority intersections throughout CD6, in addition to in-person enforcement.

y26.x: Budget for critical enforcement action throughout the district.

items.t: Promote greater access to affordable groceries
items.x: Prioritize the expansion of affordable, high-quality grocery options across CD6. Red Hook in particular faces a higher-than-average rate of food insecurity and SNAP usage, making it a key area for investment.

items.t: Improve rent affordability for small businesses
items.x: Support rent stabilization measures, vacancy taxes, and long-term lease assistance for small and legacy businesses across CD6. Encourage the preservation of discounted industrial space and affordable artist studios, particularly in Red Hook and Gowanus.
